source_caption:
Stanley Kubrick once called The Vanishing (1988) the most terrifying film he had ever seen.

According to director George Sluizer, Kubrick personally called him after watching the film and said he had seen it ten times. He was deeply impressed by its structure, its devastating ending, and Johanna ter Steege’s performance.So impressed that he reportedly offered her a role in his unmade project Aryan Papers.

When Sluizer asked him, “But you directed The Shining, haven’t you seen that?” Kubrick replied, “Yeah, but that was child’s play compared to this.”

Entertainment Weekly ranked it the 25th scariest movie of all time, and it’s also included in 1001 Movies You Must See Before You Die, edited by Steven Schneider.

source_details.synopsis: The Vanishing (Dutch: Spoorloos, literally: "Without a Trace" or "Traceless"; French: L'homme qui voulait savoir, literally: "The Man Who Wanted to Know") is a 1988 psychological thriller film co-written and directed by George Sluizer, and starring Bernard-Pierre Donnadieu, Gene Bervoets, and Johanna ter Steege in her feature film debut. The film recounts a man's obsessive years-long search for his girlfriend after she mysteriously disappears from a rest area in the French countryside. The screenplay was adapted by Sluizer and Tim Krabbé from Krabbé's 1984 novella. A co-production between the Netherlands and France, The Vanishing was filmed mostly on location in Nîmes.
